elements.char: modulation and peak frequency (Fig 7D and 7E). This is encouraging since we did not specifi-
elements.label: text

elements.char: cally aim to find a good prediction of the power spectrum when constructing the LFP proxies
elements.label: text

elements.char: and estimating their parameters. We note however that no proxy is fully able to account for the
elements.label: text

elements.char: low-frequency end of the spectrum (Fig 7A and 7B), which is overestimated by the membrane
elements.label: text

elements.char: potential proxy and underestimated by the other proxies. If one is interested in a highly
elements.label: text

elements.char: detailed reproduction of the whole LFP spectrum, preliminary results hint to the possibility of
elements.label: text

elements.char: designing a WS fit optimized to match the spectrum instead than the spatiotemporal features
elements.label: text

elements.char: and to define an LFP proxy that slightly differs from the RWS discussed above. However, the
elements.label: text

elements.char: fraction of spectral variance explained by the RWS is already 0.91 (average over all stimulus
elements.label: text

elements.char: intensities above 0.5 spikes/ms, standard morphology and synaptic condition) which likely is
elements.label: text

elements.char: sufficient for most purposes.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Model assumptions and limitations
elements.label: text

elements.char: In the present work we have focused on how the relationship between LIF variables and
elements.label: text

elements.char: ground-truth LFP change when the 3D model features change, keeping the LIF model fixed.
elements.label: text

elements.char: While different LIF networks would generate different activity and hence different synaptic
elements.label: text

elements.char: currents, we expect roughly the same relationship between these synaptic currents and the gen-
elements.label: text

elements.char: erated LFP. Therefore, for any LIF network generating enough correlated activity to result in a
elements.label: text

elements.char: sizeable LFP, we expect RWS to be a good proxy.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Our strategy had the advantage that we could vary the assumptions in the LFP-generating
elements.label: text

elements.char: model, e.g., the distribution of synapses or neuronal morphologies, without affecting the spik-
elements.label: text

elements.char: ing dynamics. The disadvantage of this approach is, however, that the 3D network does not
elements.label: text

elements.char: match the LIF network in every respect; for instance, even though the synaptic input currents
elements.label: text

elements.char: were identical in the two models, the resulting soma potentials in the multi-compartmental
elements.label: text

elements.char: neurons were not identical to those in the LIF neurons (due to passive dendritic filtering). It is,
elements.label: text

elements.char: however, unlikely that imposing identical somatic potentials, or identical currents entering the
elements.label: text

elements.char: soma, in the two models would result in a more realistic LFP since large synaptic currents
elements.label: text

elements.char: would be needed to overcome the passive filtering for distant synapses. Instead one could con-
elements.label: text

elements.char: sider changing the synaptic weight distribution in the LIF network simulation to make the two
elements.label: text

elements.char: models match better. Our focus here was to use LIF models as commonly used in the literature
elements.label: text

elements.char: (typically using homogeneous weight distributions), but it would be an interesting topic for
elements.label: text

elements.char: future studies to extract effective point-neuron synaptic weight distributions from the multi-
elements.label: text

elements.char: compartmental population and use these in the LIF network simulations in order to make the
elements.label: text

elements.char: two simulation environments even more similar.
elements.label: text

elements.char: We did not test different LIF network architectures or sizes, but we expect the RWS proxy
elements.label: text

elements.char: to be applicable as long as the network displays a sufficient level of correlation. We have found
elements.label: text

elements.char: in previous modeling studies [20,21] that correlated synaptic activity is necessary to create a
elements.label: text

elements.char: sizable LFP signal, and in this case all cells in the dominant LFP-generating population will
elements.label: text

elements.char: contribute. Making the network size larger or altering its connectivity would therefore likely
elements.label: text

elements.char: not qualitatively change the form of the best LFP proxy (as long as a sufficient level of spiking
elements.label: text

elements.char: correlations is maintained in the network). The LFP generated by larger populations, however,
elements.label: text

elements.char: should be tested in further studies taking into account the summed effect of several cortical
elements.label: text

elements.char: populations, across layers as well as heterogeneous spatial structure in the horizontal direction.
elements.label: text

elements.char: A limitation of the presented simulation setup is that it models only AMPA and GABA syn-
elements.label: text

elements.char: apse contributions. However, most of our results pertaining to the proxy do not depend on the
elements.label: text

elements.char: particular feature of the synapses and are therefore likely to extend to different synapses as
elements.label: text

elements.char: well. For instance, it should not matter for the quality of our suggested proxy whether or not
elements.label: text

elements.char: the synaptic weights are changing due to plasticity since the weight changes will be reflected in
